title: Runtime Execution Quilt: Cross-layer Handoff Patterns and Kernel Contract Reference
author: Amira Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the Execution Quilt concept — a cross-layer catalog of handoff patterns between the request dispatcher, runtime scheduler, kernel selector, and KV cache. It also specifies the kernel contract (inputs, expected invariants, telemetry tags), profiling recipes aligned to each handoff pattern, benchmark integration points, a short release note for the first quilted rollout, and an operator runbook for handoff regressions.

Audience: runtime engineers, scheduler authors, profiler/benchmark owners, oncall, and SRE.

Goals
- Provide a minimal, verifiable contract that kernel implementations must satisfy to be considered compatible with runtime handoffs.
- Enumerate canonical handoff patterns and the expected telemetry envelopes for each (latency slices, tail percentiles, cost counters).
- Prescribe profiling and benchmark steps that map a detected regression to a handoff pattern and candidate kernel faults.
- Offer an operational runbook to identify, triage, and mitigate cross-layer handoff regressions.

Design principles
1) Explicit contracts: each handoff point publishes a small JSON contract blob that contains preconditions and postconditions (see Kernel Contract section).
2) Observability-first: every handoff emits an immutable trace span with standardized tags (see Telemetry section).
3) Small surface area for kernel authors: the contract exposes only deterministic input buffers and a handful of guarded side effects.
4) Incremental rollout: new kernel variants must pass shadow-mode handoffs and a fidelity gate in the benchmark suite before canary.

Kernel Contract (reference)
- contract_id: string (human-readable, e.g., "kv-prefetch-v1")
- inputs: list of input descriptors (type, max_size_tokens, alignment)
- invariants: list of assertions the kernel must preserve (e.g., deterministic kv-cache lookups, no cross-tenant side effects)
- outputs: envelope description (token stream framing, checksum, optional compressed payload)
- error modes: canonical error codes and recommended fallbacks
- telemetry_tags: mandatory tags to be attached to the handoff span

Example (JSON contract blob):
```
{
  "contract_id": "streaming-attn-compact-v1",
  "inputs": ["kv_snapshot:base64","request_tokens:int[]","session_metadata:map"],
  "invariants": ["kv_snapshot_timestamp <= request_timestamp","no_gpu_buffer_pinning_across_sessions"],
  "outputs": ["token_chunks","final_checksum"],
  "error_modes": ["E_KV_MISS","E_KERNEL_TIMEOUT","E_CONSISTENCY"],
  "telemetry_tags": ["kernel.variant","handshake.duration_ms","kvcache.hits"]
}
```

Handoff patterns (catalog)
1) Fast-path local-kv-prefetch: Dispatcher requests a KV prefetch; kernel must accept a snapshot and return a confirmation handshake within 2ms median. Telemetry: kvcache.prefetch_ms, kvcache.prefetch_size. Fallthrough: on prefetch timeout, runtime proceeds without prefetch and marks the span tag prefetch.fallback=true.

2) Streaming-attention with slice hedging: Kernel consumes slices and emits partial tokens. The scheduler may hedged-dispatch the same request to an alternative kernel if slice latency exceeds threshold. Telemetry: slice.count, hedge.invocations, hedge.vs_primary_latency_ms.

3) Cross-tenant memory reclamation handoff: Kernel indicates an ephemeral memory pressure hint; scheduler coordinates a cooperative eviction and emits sustained backpressure signals. Telemetry: pressure.level, eviction.duration_ms.

4) Quantized-fallback handshake: Kernel advertises quantized_profile id and expected precision; if quality checks fail at output verification stage, runtime triggers a graceful fallback to a higher-precision kernel. Telemetry: quant.profile, verification.fail_count.

Telemetry & Tagging standard
Every handoff must emit a single span named "handoff.<contract_id>" with these tags:
- kernel.variant (string)
- kernel.commit (short sha)
- handoff.duration_ms (integer)
- handoff.stage (one of: prefetch, accept, execute, finalize)
- kvcache.hits (integer)
- request.surface_id (string)
- fidelity.score (float, optional)

Profiling playbook mapped to handoff patterns
- When to use: run this playbook whenever a latency or fidelity regression is localized to the post-dispatch horizon (i.e., after request routing and admission).
- Tools: native tracer (TRACE-RT), kernel microprofiler (kmprof), sampling proxy (shadow-agent), replay harness (req-replay).

Profiling steps (ordered)
1) Reproduce in shadow: enable shadow-mode for the suspect kernel and collect full traces for N=500 requests sampled from the offending cohort.
2) Isolate handoff spans: filter traces for spans named "handoff.*" and sort by handoff.duration_ms 95th percentile.
3) Run kmprof on the top 20 slow handoff traces to collect per-instruction latency and GPU stall regions.
4) Correlate with scheduler telemetry: pull scheduler slot allocations and preemption events for the same time window.
5) Differential trace: replay the same request on a known-good kernel variant and produce a diff report.
6) If kernel microprobes point to memory-copy hot loops, instrument kernel with optional pinned-buffer mode and rerun.

Profiling example command set
- Enable shadow traces: ./opsctl handoff-shadow enable --contract streaming-attn-compact-v1 --duration 2h
- Extract handoff spans: tracer-cli query --span-filter "name:handoff.* AND tag:surface_id=chat_v1" --p95 --out handoff_p95.json
- Run kmprof (GPU): kmprof record --trace-file handoff_p95.json --out kmprof_top20.kmp

Benchmark integration points
- Add a handoff-focused benchmark to the microbenchmark suite (bench/handshake) that exercises: prefetch, slice hedging, quantized fallback, and memory pressure signals.
- Performance matrix: for each kernel variant, report median p50/p95 handoff.duration_ms, handshake success rate, and end-to-end delta vs baseline.

Suggested benchmark table (text):
| kernel_variant | p50_handoff_ms | p95_handoff_ms | handshake_success_pct | e2e_delta_ms |
|----------------|----------------|----------------|-----------------------|-------------:|
| streaming-attn-compact-v1 | 1.2 | 6.8 | 99.5 | +3 |
| streaming-attn-compact-v2 | 0.9 | 5.3 | 99.7 | +1 |

Release notes (excerpt): Execution Quilt rollout v0.9.3
- 2026-11-12: Introduced kernel contract enforcement at admission time and new handoff telemetry tags.
- 2026-11-19: Added bench/handshake microbenchmark to CI and a canary gate requiring <10% p95 increase across candidate shards.
- Rollout notes: v0.9.3 was deployed to 10% of traffic for dedicated pools; two regressions (one in quantized-fallback path, one due to ephemeral nvlink contention) were caught by the handoff p95 gate and rolled back before canary expansion.

Runbook: handoff regression triage (operator steps)
1) Detect: alert threshold = 2x baseline p95_handoff_ms for a surface for >=10 minutes.
2) Contain: shift new requests for the surface to fallback route (runtime config: route.fidelity=stable) and enable hedged dispatch disabled for the surface.
3) Collect: run the profiling steps above for 30-60 minutes and upload kmprof artifacts to /artifacts/handoff-regressions/<incident-id>.
4) Mitigate: pin the surface to the previous kernel by contract_id using opsctl: ./opsctl kernel-pin set --surface chat_v1 --contract streaming-attn-compact-v1 --until 2026-11-30
5) Postmortem: publish incident page with root cause, timeframe, and a remediation plan.

Known issues (current list)
- NI-2026-115: Intermittent handshake delay when large kv_snapshot (>4MB serialized) is provided to compact kernels. Workaround: enable incremental-kv-prefetch on large sessions.
- NI-2026-127: Hedge count mismatch between dispatcher and kernel under extreme queueing (observed at >95th percentile load). Mitigation: tune hedge.max_attempts to 1 for vulnerable surfaces.

Open mitigations and action items
1) Introduce an incremental prefetch protocol to split large snapshots; owner: kernel-team; ETA: 2027-01-15.
2) Add handoff p99 to the bench/handshake matrix; owner: perf-suite; ETA: 2026-12-31.
3) Formalize a test harness that simulates NVLink fluctuations and measures handshake success rate; owner: infra-performance; ETA: 2027-02-01.

Appendix A — Quick-check list for kernel authors (pre-submit)
1) Include a contract_id and attach a small example contract JSON in your PR.
2) Add mandatory telemetry tags to your kernel code paths.
3) Run bench/handshake locally and ensure p95_handoff_ms <= baseline * 1.10.
4) Provide a graceful fallback path (documented error codes).

Appendix B — Short glossary
- Handoff: the deterministic exchange between runtime layers when control for a request transitions to a kernel or other execution unit.
- Contract: immutable descriptor of expected inputs, invariants, outputs, and telemetry for a kernel.
- Hedge: a speculative duplicate dispatch intended to reduce tail latency.
